trap-nonspeakable.notes: RIGOR. VERIFIED CORRECT: sigma(f + sigma f) = sigma f + sigma^2 f = f + sigma f and sigma(f - sigma f) = sigma f - f = -(f - sigma f), using sigma^2 = id, so the displayed identity and both parity claims hold over any commutative ring exactly as stated. ONE MINOR OVERCLAIM: 'The decomposition is unique and holds over any commutative ring.' EXISTENCE holds over any commutative ring; UNIQUENESS needs 2 to be a non-zero-divisor. Counterexample: R = Z/2 with sigma = id. There every element is simultaneously bar-even and bar-odd (since -1 = 1), and 0 = 2f decomposes both as (0, 0) and as (1, 1) with 1 even and 1 odd — two distinct (even, odd) pairs. In general the difference of two decompositions is killed only by 2, so uniqueness is exactly the statement that 2 is a non-zero-divisor. Proposed: 'The decomposition holds over any commutative ring, and is unique whenever 2 is a non-zero-divisor.' Worth stating because the block explicitly advertises maximal generality, and the Lean carrier (QOU.QBeta.bar_parity_decomposition) will need the same hypothesis if it claims uniqueness.
